models.name: economic_board_categories
models.description:
System-defined categories for tagging and filtering discussion posts.

Contains the predefined set of topics used to classify and search content on the economic and political discussion board. These categories are immutable core system values that enable consistent tagging and filtering across the platform. Citizens can filter posts by these categories, and moderators use them to organize content.

Each category has a human-readable name and a unique code used in API calls and search queries. Change to this list requires administrator-level deployment and is not editable by users or moderators through the UI.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable name of the category (e.g., "economy", "politics"). Must be unique within the system.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Machine-readable code identifier for the category (e.g., "economy", "politics"). Must be unique and used in search and filtering APIs.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the category's scope and usage guidelines. Used for internal documentation and moderator reference.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was last updated. System field maintained automatically.

models.name: economic_board_system_config
models.description:
Global configuration settings for the economic board platform.

Stores critical system-wide parameters that control the behavior, limits, and features of the discussion board. These are configuration values that determine how the system operates, such as character limits, time windows, and feature toggles.

This table serves as the single source of truth for all system configuration parameters. Modifications require administrative access and should be made with extreme caution as they affect all users. Values are read by the application during runtime to enforce business rules and behavioral constraints.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Configuration key name (e.g., "comment_max_length", "edit_window_hours"). Must be unique.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: JSON-serialized value of the configuration setting (e.g., "500", "24", "true"). Can be string, number, boolean, or complex JSON object.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this configuration controls and its business purpose.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last modified. System field maintained automatically.

models.name: economic_board_timezone_settings
models.description:
Timezone configuration for user-facing timestamp display.

Contains supported timezone identifiers that the system uses to convert UTC timestamps to local time for display to users. The system stores all timestamps internally in UTC, but presents them in the user's local timezone.

This table ensures consistency in time representation across the platform. The system endpoint for user timezone registration uses values from this table to validate user selections. Only timezones listed here can be selected by users.

The primary timezone ("Asia/Seoul") is pre-configured and required for the system to function correctly in the target market.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Full timezone name from the IANA timezone database (e.g., "Asia/Seoul", "America/New_York"). Must be a valid timezone identifier.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Short identifier for the timezone (e.g., "KST", "EST"). Used for display in the UI where space is limited.

plainFields.name: offset
plainFields.description: UTC offset in format +09:00 or -05:00 representing the timezone difference from UTC.

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this timezone is the system default (true) or an optional selection (false). Exactly one record should have is_default=true.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timezone setting was added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timezone setting was last modified. System field maintained automatically.

models.name: economic_board_content_flags
models.description:
System-defined content flag categories for automated and manual moderation.

Contains categories of content violations that trigger automated detection or manual moderation actions. These flags are used to identify potentially problematic posts such as hate speech, threats, doxxing, or false information.

When a post is flagged by automated systems or user reports, a matching flag from this table is applied to trigger moderation workflows. Each flag defines the violation type, severity level, and automated handling rules.

This table serves as the authoritative reference for moderation systems and must be maintained with care by administrators.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable name of the content flag category (e.g., "hate_speech", "doxxing"). Must be unique.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Machine-readable code identifier for the flag (e.g., "hate_speech", "doxxing"). Used by detection systems and moderation APIs.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of the violation: "low", "medium", or "high". Determines automated response and moderator priority.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of what types of content this flag identifies and examples of violations.

plainFields.name: auto_flag_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this flag type is actively monitored by automated detection systems.

plainFields.name: auto_reject_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether posts flagged with this type should be automatically rejected (instead of just flagged for review).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this flag type was added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this flag type was last modified. System field maintained automatically.

models.name: economic_board_citizens
models.description:
Core identity record for citizens who participate in economic and political discussions.

Each citizen has a unique, persistent account that links all their posts, comments, attachments, warnings, and moderation history. This table stores authentication credentials and account status metadata.

Citizens initiate content creation and interaction, requiring authentication and authorization. This table serves as the authoritative source for citizen identity and ban/suspension status within the system.

The relationship to citizen_sessions is one-to-many. Each citizen can have multiple active sessions concurrently via different devices or browsing contexts.

Account deletion triggers anonymization of content ({@link economic_board_posts}, {@link economic_board_comments}) while preserving audit trail integrity.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Citizen's contact email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique and verified before posting content.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication using bcrypt algorithm. Never stores plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this citizen account was created. Always reflects the system's UTC clock.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this citizen account record. Updated on password changes, profile edits, or status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this citizen account was deleted. When not null, the account is considered deleted and inaccessible. Null indicates active account.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current account status. Valid values: 'active', 'suspended', 'banned'. Suspended (3 warnings) temporarily blocks posting. Banned (3 suspensions) permanently blocks all activity.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated citizen sessions.

Tracks active connections from citizens to the platform using JWT authentication. Each record represents a single login session from a specific device, browser, or IP address.

Sessions are managed purely by the authentication service and are not directly manipulated by citizens. They are automatically expired based on timeout policies and invalidated during logout or password changes.

All required fields match the session table specification exactly. No additional fields are permitted. This table does not store tokens, user agent, or device information.

Relationship to economic_board_citizens is many-to-one: one citizen can have many active sessions concurrently.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen this session belongs to. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which this session was initiated. Used for security monitoring and abuse detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page from which the user initiated the login session. Used for traffic origin analysis.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to the login page. Used for marketing and user acquisition analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created and the JWT token was issued. This is the authoritative start time of the session.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session will expire. If null, the session has not yet been explicitly expired through logout or password change. When null, the session may be manually invalidated.

models.name: economic_board_moderators
models.description:
Core identity record for moderators who administrate and oversee economic and political discussion content.

Each moderator has a unique, persistent account that links all their moderation actions, warnings issued, posts approved or rejected, and audit logs. This table stores authentication credentials and account status metadata.

Moderators are granted elevated privileges to manage content integrity and enforce community guidelines. This table serves as the authoritative source for moderator identity and activity within the system.

The relationship to moderator_sessions is one-to-many. Each moderator can have multiple active sessions concurrently via different devices or browsing contexts.

Moderator accounts are created only by administrators and cannot be self-signed up. Account deletion is not permitted - only deactivation via status change.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Moderator's contact email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique and verified during account creation.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication using bcrypt algorithm. Never stores plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderator account was created. Always reflects the system's UTC clock.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this moderator account record. Updated on password changes or status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderator account was deactivated. Cannot be truly deleted per business rules - only deactivated via status field. When not null, the account is effectively disabled.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current account status. Valid values: 'active', 'deactivated'. When 'deactivated', the moderator can no longer authenticate and perform any moderator actions. No permanent deletion of moderator accounts permitted.

models.name: economic_board_moderator_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated moderator sessions.

Tracks active connections from moderators to the platform using JWT authentication. Each record represents a single login session from a specific device, browser, or IP address.

Sessions are managed purely by the authentication service and are not directly manipulated by moderators. They are automatically expired based on timeout policies and invalidated during logout or password changes.

All required fields match the session table specification exactly. No additional fields are permitted. This table does not store tokens, user agent, or device information.

Relationship to economic_board_moderators is many-to-one: one moderator can have many active sessions concurrently.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator this session belongs to. {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which this session was initiated. Used for security monitoring and abuse detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page from which the user initiated the login session. Used for traffic origin analysis.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to the login page. Used for marketing and user acquisition analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created and the JWT token was issued. This is the authoritative start time of the session.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session will expire. If null, the session has not yet been explicitly expired through logout or password change. When null, the session may be manually invalidated.

models.name: economic_board_posts
models.description:
Main discussion posts submitted by citizens, subject to moderation.

Represents the primary content entities on the economic/political board. Posts are created by authenticated citizens and must pass moderation review before becoming publicly visible.

Each post has a lifecycle: initially "pending" (invisible to citizens), then either "published" (publicly visible) or "rejected" (archived). Moderators can delete published posts, which sets the deleted_at timestamp.

The 24-hour editing window is enforced via the post_revisions table. A post can only be edited within 24 hours of creation and edits are tracked separately to preserve original content.

Post status directly controls visibility: only published posts appear in feeds, search results, and category filters. Rejected posts are never shown.

Related to citizens via the citizen_id foreign key and to post_revisions via one-to-many relationship. Attachments are managed via economic_board_attachment_logs referencing this post's ID.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who created this post. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_approved_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who approved this post. Nullable if not yet approved or if rejected. {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_rejected_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who rejected this post. Nullable if not rejected. {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_deleted_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who permanently deleted this post. Nullable unless deleted. {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: The category tag assigned to this post for search and filtering. {@link economic_board_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The title of the discussion post, up to 10,000 characters. Mandatory field.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: The main content of the discussion post, up to 10,000 characters. Mandatory field.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current visibility state of the post. Valid values: 'pending', 'published', 'rejected'. Initially defaulting to 'pending' upon creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was originally created and submitted by the citizen. Always set by system in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the post's metadata (status, moderation decisions). Does not include edits tracked in post_revisions table.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was permanently deleted by a moderator. If null, the post is not deleted. For audit purposes.

models.name: economic_board_post_revisions
models.description:
Historical record of post edits made within the 24-hour editing window.

Records each edit a citizen makes to their post within 24 hours of its initial submission. Used to preserve original content and enable "edited" labels.

Each revision is immutable and stored as a complete snapshot. Only citizens can create revisions, and only within the 24-hour window. After this window, no revisions are created.

Completes the 24-hour editing capability for posts. The system uses this table to display "Edited" indicators without modifying the main economic_board_posts.record.

This table is subsidiary - it cannot exist without a corresponding post, and is never accessed directly by UI clients.

Linked to economic_board_posts by post_id.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: The parent post being revised. Must exist. {@link economic_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who made this revision. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title version at the time of this edit. Same as post.title if unchanged.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Content version at the time of this edit. Same as post.body if unchanged.

plainFields.name: edited_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this revision was saved. Must be within 24 hours of the post's created_at timestamp.

models.name: economic_board_comments
models.description:
User comments attached to published discussion posts.

Allows citizens to respond directly to published posts. Comments appear immediately upon submission and are visible to all users.

Comments are primary entities: citizens need to manage them independently (edit within 24 hours, delete their own, view all comments they've made). Posts can have many comments, and comments can be moderated independently of their parent post.

Comments have their own 24-hour editing window, separate from the post's window. After 24 hours, comments cannot be edited.

Comments cannot be posted on pending or rejected posts. Only published posts are commentable.

Comments respect thread integrity: if a post is deleted, comments remain visible with "[Original post removed]" indicator.

Subject to character limits: each comment is limited to 500 characters (enforced at application layer).

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: The published post this comment replies to. Must reference a post with status 'published'. {@link economic_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who wrote this comment. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_comment_id
foreignFields.description: If this is a reply to another comment, references the parent comment. For thread nesting. {@link economic_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_deleted_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who deleted this comment. Nullable unless deleted. {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: The content of the comment, up to 500 characters. Required and non-nullable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was submitted. Always set by system in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last edit to the comment (within 24-hour window), or field update. Does not include deletion time.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was permanently deleted by a moderator. If null, the comment is not deleted. For audit and thread integrity.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current visibility state of the comment. Valid values: 'published', 'deleted'. Initially 'published'. Moderators set to 'deleted'.

models.name: economic_board_attachments
models.description:
Stores metadata for all file attachments uploaded to discussion posts.

Represents the authoritative record of each file attached to a post. This is a primary entity that is created when a user uploads a file and accessed when serving attachments to users or moderators. The system enforces file size (≤10MB) and format restrictions (JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, TXT, DOCX, XLSX) at upload time. Attachments are never deleted permanently—only soft-deleted to preserve audit trails. Attachment data is persistent even if the parent post is deleted, as required for compliance.

Each attachment is linked to exactly one post. Attachment metadata includes original filename, sanitized name, storage location, file size, MIME type, and current status (uploaded, processed, quarantined). This table is referenced directly by the posts table and is accessed via API to serve file downloads or display file previews.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post this attachment is linked to. {@link economic_board_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: original_name
plainFields.description: The original filename as uploaded by the user.

plainFields.name: sanitized_name
plainFields.description: The sanitized filename after removing special characters (only alphanumeric, hyphen, underscore, period allowed).

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Enforced to be ≤ 10MB (10485760 bytes) during upload.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Verified against allowed formats on upload: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: The unique, securely signed URI where the file is stored in object storage. Cannot be a direct path; must use signed, time-limited endpoints for access.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the attachment. Values: 'uploaded' (after initial upload), 'processed' (after validation), 'quarantined' (if flagged for malware or blocked format). Never delete, only transition between these states.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment record was first created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was last modified (e.g., status change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attachment was soft-deleted. NULL means active. Used solely for audit and retrieval—not for access control. System retains attachments for 180 days after deletion.

models.name: economic_board_attachment_logs
models.description:
Tracks all changes made to attachment records for audit compliance.

This subsidiary table records every action performed on an attachment—specifically status changes, metadata updates, and deletion events. It is automatically populated by system processes and admin actions, never by direct user input. Required to meet audit trail requirements for 180-day retention and mandatory transparency in moderation actions.

Each log entry records the attachment ID (foreign key), the actor responsible (moderator or system), the action performed, and the before/after values of affected fields. Real-time updates to attachment status (e.g., from 'uploaded' to 'processed') are logged here. This table is referenced only by the attachment table and never accessed directly by frontend UI, only by moderation or compliance systems.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: The attachment this log entry refers to. {@link economic_board_attachments.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed the action (if applicable). NULL if action triggered by system (e.g., automated scan). {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who originally uploaded the file, for context. May be needed for notifications. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: The operation performed. Values: 'uploaded', 'processed', 'quarantined', 'deleted', 'status_changed'.

plainFields.name: field_changed
plainFields.description: The specific field that was changed, if any (e.g., 'status', 'file_size', 'mime_type'). NULL if no field changed but action occurred (e.g., 'deleted').

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: The previous value of the field_changed, stored as stringified JSON for generality. E.g., '{"status": "uploaded"}'. NULL if no prior value (e.g., on creation).

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: The new value of the field_changed, stored as stringified JSON for generality. E.g., '{"status": "processed"}'.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Free-form description of why the action was taken (e.g., 'File exceeded size limit', 'Malware detected', 'Moderator approval'). Required for moderator-initiated changes; optional for system actions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this log entry was created. Always matches when the change occurred.

models.name: economic_board_moderation_actions
models.description:
Central record of all moderation actions performed on the economic board.

This is the primary audit entity that captures the metadata of all moderation actions including warnings, deletions, and locks. Each action record is linked to exactly one specific type of action through the subtype tables, ensuring database-level integrity and avoiding nullable fields.

All moderation activities originate from this table, which is accessed by moderators on their dashboard to review and manage community content. The table tracks who performed the action, when it occurred, and provides the context for the specific moderation event.

Subtype tables (warnings, deletions, locks) extend this base record with domain-specific data.

Each action can be associated with a citizen (target) and a moderator (actor), creating a complete audit trail. The deleted_at field allows for reversible actions and audit retention in compliance with platform policy.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen targeted by this moderation action. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed this action. {@link economic_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this moderation action was initiated. Always non-null.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this moderation action was last modified. Always non-null.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this moderation action was logically deleted. Null if still active. Required for audit trail retention of all actions per policy.

models.name: economic_board_moderation_warnings
models.description:
Specific record for warning actions issued to citizens for policy violations.

This subsidiary table captures detailed information about each warning issued to a citizen. Each warning record is linked via a 1:1 relationship to a main moderation action, ensuring that every warning has exactly one associated audit record in economic_board_moderation_actions.

Warnings are tracked per citizen to enforce the policy of suspending users after three active warnings. Each warning entry includes the reason given by the moderator, providing transparency to the citizen.

The attached moderation action record (in economic_board_moderation_actions) contains the timestamps and moderator information. This table is exclusively accessed through its parent action record and never independently managed by users.

No other fields are needed as all required context is already captured in the parent table and through the foreign key relationship to citizens.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The main moderation action record that this warning extends. 1:1 relationship with economic_board_moderation_actions. {@link economic_board_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The specific reason given by the moderator for issuing this warning. Must be at least 10 characters as required by policy. Required for transparency and audit.

plainFields.name: warning_count_on_issue
plainFields.description: The number of active warnings the citizen had at the time this warning was issued. Used to trigger suspension when reaching three warnings.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this warning was issued. Mirrors the parent action's created_at and maintained for consistency.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this warning was last updated. Mirrors the parent action's updated_at and maintained for consistency.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this warning was logically deleted. Null if still active. Required for audit trail retention of all actions per policy.

models.name: economic_board_moderation_deletions
models.description:
Specific record for post or comment deletions performed by moderators.

This subsidiary table captures detailed information about each deletion action taken by a moderator. Each deletion record is linked via a 1:1 relationship to a main moderation action, ensuring that every deletion has exactly one associated audit record in economic_board_moderation_actions.

Deletions are tracked to ensure transparency to citizens who had their content removed and to provide an audit trail for compliance. This table stores the reason for deletion and the specific content affected (via foreign key in the parent table).

The attached moderation action record (in economic_board_moderation_actions) contains the timestamps and moderator information. This table is exclusively accessed through its parent action record and never independently managed by users.

No other fields are needed as all required context is already captured in the parent table and through the foreign key relationship to content entities.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The main moderation action record that this deletion extends. 1:1 relationship with economic_board_moderation_actions. {@link economic_board_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The specific reason given by the moderator for this deletion. Must be at least 10 characters as required by policy. Required for transparency and audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this deletion was performed. Mirrors the parent action's created_at and maintained for consistency.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this deletion was last updated. Mirrors the parent action's updated_at and maintained for consistency.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this deletion was logically deleted. Null if still active. Required for audit trail retention of all actions per policy.

models.name: economic_board_moderation_locks
models.description:
Specific record for discussion threads locked by moderators to prevent further comments.

This subsidiary table captures detailed information about each thread lock action performed by a moderator. Each lock record is linked via a 1:1 relationship to a main moderation action, ensuring that every lock has exactly one associated audit record in economic_board_moderation_actions.

Thread locks are used to prevent further comments on contentious discussions while preserving the existing conversation history. This table stores a custom message explaining the lock reason, which is displayed on the locked thread.

The attached moderation action record (in economic_board_moderation_actions) contains the timestamps and moderator information. This table is exclusively accessed through its parent action record and never independently managed by users.

No other fields are needed as all required context is already captured in the parent table and through the foreign key relationship to the target post.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The main moderation action record that this lock extends. 1:1 relationship with economic_board_moderation_actions. {@link economic_board_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: lock_message
plainFields.description: The message displayed to users when a thread is locked. This can be customized by the moderator to explain the reason (e.g., 'Discussion closed due to personal attacks'). Must be clear and comply with transparency policy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this lock was applied. Mirrors the parent action's created_at and maintained for consistency.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this lock was last updated. Mirrors the parent action's updated_at and maintained for consistency.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this lock was logically removed. Null if still active. Required for audit trail retention of all actions per policy.

models.name: economic_board_search_metadata
models.description:
Denormalized search metadata for economic board posts.

Stores searchable fields from primary posts for optimized query performance. This table is updated asynchronously from the economic_board_posts table to avoid impacting transaction performance during content creation. Contains pre-computed fields used by full-text search engines to return results under 2 seconds.

Data fields include the post title, content, and derived metadata like word count and sentiment score. This table enables fast keyword searches across thousands of posts without burdening the main transactional table with indexing overhead.

Search metadata is not intended for direct user interaction but serves as the backbone of the post discovery system. Updates are triggered by changes to the main economic_board_posts table.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the primary post this search metadata describes. {@link economic_board_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The title of the post being indexed for search. Copied from economic_board_posts.title.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The full text content of the post being indexed for search. Copied from economic_board_posts.content.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current status of the related post: 'pending', 'published', or 'rejected'. Used to filter search results.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this search metadata record was generated. Matches economic_board_posts.created_at, but stored here for search efficiency.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this search metadata record was last updated. Updates when the main post is edited or status changes.

plainFields.name: word_count
plainFields.description: Total number of words in the post content. Pre-calculated to avoid runtime computation during search.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: Whether the related post has been locked by a moderator. Used to exclude locked discussions from search result relevance scoring.

models.name: economic_board_search_tags
models.description:
Tags associated with search metadata for efficient filtering and tagging-based discovery.

This table links search metadata records with predefined categories, allowing for fast filtering of search results by topic. Each entry represents a single tag association for a specific post.

Tags are derived from economic_board_categories and associated via economic_board_search_metadata. This denormalized structure avoids expensive JOIN operations during search queries.

The primary use is for category-based filters such as "economy", "politics", and "markets". This table enables instant display of what categories a post belongs to during search and discovery.

Each record represents one tag per post, so multiple records may exist for articles with multiple tags.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_search_metadata_id
foreignFields.description: References the search metadata record this tag is associated with. {@link economic_board_search_metadata.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_category_id
foreignFields.description: References the category this tag belongs to. {@link economic_board_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this tag association was created. Matches the timestamp of the original post's publication or update.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this tag association was last updated, usually when the main post was edited or category changed.

models.name: economic_board_search_index
models.description:
Full-text search index for economic board posts.

This table provides an optimized, denormalized structure for high-performance full-text keyword searching across the entire economic board. It contains precomputed word vectors from post titles and content to enable complex text searches with results under 2 seconds.

The index is generated by processing the text from economic_board_posts content and title fields, eliminating stop words and applying stemming. Contains text chunks split into searchable units with positional weighting.

This table is the most important performance component of the search system — it must be updated immediately whenever a post's content changes, and queried directly without joining to other tables during search operations.

The structure supports advanced queries: multilingual text matching, fuzzy matching, and relevance ranking. This is the intrinsic engine behind the search functionality.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the primary post this index entry is built from. {@link economic_board_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: tokens
plainFields.description: A concatenated string of normalized, normalized, and stemmed word tokens from the post title and content. Used for full-text search matching.

plainFields.name: word_frequencies
plainFields.description: A normalized JSON string containing frequency counts for each searchable word in the post content, including positioning weights.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this search index entry was generated or last updated. Matches the publication or last edit time of the post.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this index was last updated due to a change in the source post.
